content: Approximately one-third of individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia or related serious mental illnesses are parents. Both these parents and their children face an elevated risk of negative outcomes due to the impact of the parental mental illness. Parenting interventions have been shown to enhance parenting skills and reduce disruptive behaviors in children. This systematic review was conducted to evaluate the evidence for parenting interventions specifically designed for parents with schizophrenia or related serious mental illnesses. The objective of this review was to assess the effects of parenting interventions for individuals with schizophrenia or related serious mental illnesses. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted on February 10, 2021, using the Cochrane Schizophrenia Group's Study-Based Register of Trials. This register includes data from multiple sources, such as the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov, Embase, ISRCTN, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, PubMed, and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform. The review included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared parenting interventions to control conditions for individuals with schizophrenia or related serious mental illnesses who had children aged 0 to 18 years. The process involved independently screening citations, selecting studies, extracting data, and assessing the quality of the studies. The risk of bias in the included studies was also evaluated. Only one trial, involving 50 participants, met the inclusion criteria. However, it was not possible to extract meaningful data from this trial because the authors did not provide the necessary means and standard deviations for the outcomes of interest. Instead, they only reported whether the outcomes were statistically significant at the 0.05 level. Furthermore, three domains of this trial were assessed as having a high risk of bias. The findings from this single trial were inconclusive, and there is insufficient evidence to provide recommendations for individuals with schizophrenia or related serious mental illnesses, their clinicians, or policymakers. Although no robust RCT evidence currently exists, parenting interventions for this population have been developed. Future research should focus on testing these interventions in well-designed RCTs to strengthen the evidence base and better support this population.
